rinna.title: Tethered Clouds

image.comp: crouched on a ship's quarterdeck above the clouds fitting a wooden bench into place with a spanner in one hand, bright carefree grin
image.setting: open-air cliffside quarterdeck bar of The Skyhook Tavern

rinna.text:
The whole of the Cliffside Docks watched the old ship go up that evening. Since then every tavern on the moorings has been waiting to see her cast off for good. There's a book running on it. The favourite is 'before the autumn gales'.

So it surprises people to see what Rinna is doing this morning. She is up on the quarterdeck with a spanner and a mouthful of bolts, and she is fixing a bench to the planking. It's a long bench for customers, and it faces the view.

"Tobbin asked me when I'm selling up and flying south," she says around the bolts. She spits one into her palm and drives it home. "I told him I flew for sixty years, and I never had a home port. There wasn't one to come back to." She sits back on her heels and spins the spanner over her thumb. Her tail is swinging. "There's no decent rum up in the clouds. And there's no boss up there mad enough to fly a tavern with me. I checked."

choices.label: Promise her a flight day whenever the skies clear
choices.res: You promise her a flight day, whenever the sky is clear and the bar can spare her. Her tail thumps the hull boards hard enough to shake the bench. "I'll hold you to that, captain-on-paper," she says. "First clear morning. You're taking the wheel for the landing, too. It's time you learned what your own building does."

choices.label: Help her anchor the storm awning before gale season
choices.res: The two of you rig the storm awning over the deck bar before the gales come. It takes half an hour, a great deal of knotted line, and every piece of sailor's language she knows. When it's done she hangs her full weight off the ridge rope to test it. It doesn't move. "There," she says. "She'll ride out a hurricane. So will the rum."

rinna.title: Harbor Horizon

image.comp: leaning on a ship's taffrail at midnight holding out an uncorked bottle, lanterns swinging overhead, warm teasing smile
image.setting: starlit cliffside deck of The Skyhook above harbor lights

2.text:
The lanterns are swinging on their lines above the quarterdeck. The fog has come in under the hull, so that the Skyhook seems to be floating on it. The bar closed an hour ago.

Rinna pulls the cork out of her best bottle with her teeth and spits it over the rail. Her tricorn is hanging on the binnacle. Her shirt has slipped off one sun-brown shoulder, and she hasn't pulled it back up.

"I hauled crates through sleet for sixty years," she says. She comes around the wheel and stands very close to you, and her tail curls around the back of your knee. "There was brandy and silk, and other people's gold. Once it was a whole brass band." Her slit pupils have gone wide in the lantern light. "The best cargo I ever landed walked up that gangway by itself, in a grey hoodie, with a deed in its hand. The captain's bunk is right below us, boss. I checked the ropes on it this morning."

image.comp: standing very close beside a ship's wheel with an uncorked bottle in one hand, tail curled behind his knee, wide slit pupils, wicked teasing grin
image.setting: foggy quarterdeck of The Skyhook under swinging lanterns
image.wear: an open white shirt slipping off one shoulder

rinna.text:
The lanterns are swinging on their lines above the quarterdeck. The fog has come in under the hull, so that the Skyhook seems to be floating on it. The bar closed an hour ago.

Rinna is leaning on the wheel. She has a bottle of the spiced rum, and she passes it to you across the spokes without wiping the neck.

"I chased horizons for sixty years," she says. "You know what happens when you reach one? There's another. You'd think someone would have warned me." She takes the bottle back and drinks. "I used to feel sorry for harbour folk. I'd see the same faces on the same dock every time I came in, and I'd think, you poor bastards." She looks down the length of the deck at the benches and the awning and the lantern on the bowsprit. "It's a funny thing. The anchorage was the part worth keeping. I had to run aground to find that out."

choices.label: Take her below to the captain's bunk
choices.res: Rinna hooks two claws under your chin, very lightly. She grins and walks you backward across the deck and down the cabin stair, and she doesn't once look where she's going.

else.res: You stand at the rail together and watch the night freighters cross the cove with their lamps lit. She names each ship by its rigging and tells you what it's really carrying. Neither of you goes below. When the sun comes up it turns the fog pink, and she takes off her hat to look at it.

choices.label: Challenge her to a tally of tall tales till dawn
choices.res: You trade tall tales until dawn and keep a tally on the deck in chalk. Every third story of hers has a sea monster in it, and it's a different one each time. By breakfast every dent in the hull has two new explanations. You have lost by eleven, and you don't believe a word of it.

maris.title: Salt and Wildflowers

image.comp: kneeling beside a steaming marble basin arranging fresh highland wildflowers into jade bowls, serene delighted expression
image.setting: quiet iridescent cavern hall inside The Pearl Grotto

maris.text:
Maris goes out once a week now. She takes the harbour stair in the morning and the coast road after it, and she comes back at dusk.

She never says where she has been. She doesn't need to, because she brings it back with her. There's a row of things along the rim of the jade pool. It has grown every week since the Bell went quiet: wildflowers in a cup, a spruce cone, three grey stones from a streambed, and a feather.

Tonight she has a branch of pine. She is kneeling at the pool's edge, running the needles through her fingers and holding them up to her face.

"I had three centuries of tide and stone," she says. "That was everything I could hear, and everything I could smell." She breathes in. "I had forgotten that earth could be so loud. There was a field today that had a smell, Sam. The whole field did. I stood in it until a farmer asked whether I was unwell."

choices.label: Offer to hike the ridge trail with her next off-day
choices.res: You offer to walk the ridge trail with her on her next day out. Her silver eyes brighten, and it shows even through the steam. "I shall hold you to that," she says. "I want to see the tops of the cedars. I have only ever seen the roots, where they come down through the rock. I should like to know what they've been doing up there."

choices.label: Steep one of her mountain herbs into the warm side pool
choices.res: You steep a handful of her mountain herbs in the warm side pool. Pine and salt go up together in the steam and drift across the whole cave. By nightfall the regulars are asking what has been done to the air. Maris tells each of them something different, and none of it is true. She seems to be enjoying herself a great deal.

maris.title: Silent Tide

image.comp: floating on her back in a glowing sea-cave pool under soft pearl light, long wet hair fanned out on the water, serene contented smile
image.setting: lantern-lit private turquoise tide pool inside The Pearl Grotto

2.text:
The pearls have dimmed themselves for the night. They glow a low blue over the tide pool, and the Grotto is so quiet that you can hear the water moving against the stone.

Maris comes up out of it right beside the marble stair where you are standing. The water runs off her bare shoulders and down between her tits. Her wet hair clings to her all the way to the waist. She doesn't reach for the cloth on the step.

"There's no bell," she says softly. "I have been listening for an hour, to be sure. There is nothing ringing anywhere in the dark." She holds out her hand to you across the water, palm up. "I kept watch in this pool for three hundred years, Sam. I should like to be in it for another reason tonight. Come in. There is no bargain, and the sea wants nothing for it. I do. I would rather show you what."

image.comp: rising out of the tide pool beside a marble stair, water running down her bare shoulders, wet hair clinging to her waist, palm held up toward him

maris.text:
The pearls have dimmed themselves for the night. They glow a low blue over the tide pool, and the Grotto is so quiet that you can hear the water moving against the stone.

Maris is floating on her back in the middle of it. Her sea-green hair has spread out around her. Her eyes are closed.

She knows you are there. She always does.

"I used to listen for it," she says. "I listened every night for three hundred years, in case the Bell stirred. I would lie in the water like this, and I wasn't resting. I was keeping watch." She opens her eyes and looks up at the roof. "There's nothing down there now. I can leave by that stair whenever I like, and I do. I come back down it every evening." She turns her head on the water and looks at you. "It is a different thing to stay in a place when you are the one who holds the key. I hadn't known how different it would be."

choices.label: Slip down into the warm glowing pool beside her
choices.res: You go down the steps. The warm salt water comes up around your ribs, and Maris glides in against your chest. She puts her mouth on yours and takes her time.

else.res: You lie back on the warm shelf of stone in the shallows and listen to the tide moving in the cave. She floats nearby. Neither of you speaks. Every tired muscle you have lets go, one after another, and when you wake the pearls are bright again and it is morning.

choices.label: Sit at the water's edge trading quiet histories
choices.res: You sit with your feet in the water and trade histories. You tell her about a city with no stars. She tells you one story about her past, and for the first time it stays the same from beginning to end. You catch it, and she sees that you have. She smiles down at the pool. "That one I shall only tell you," she says.

brynna.title: Square Beams

image.comp: planing a thick oak bar counter with steady calloused hands, carpentry chalk behind one ear, satisfied gruff smirk
image.setting: newly rebuilt timber gallery of Ironwood Hall

brynna.text:
There isn't a sealed wing left in Ironwood Hall. Every room is open and warm and paying for itself. As far as anyone else can see, the work is done.

You find Brynna in the upper corridor at dawn anyway. She has one of the parlor doors off its hinges and laid across two trestles, and she is taking a steel rasp to the edge of it. It was sticking. It stuck by about the thickness of a playing card, and you'd never have noticed. She did, and it has been bothering her for a week.

She rehangs it and swings it. It shuts with a flat, soft click.

"Three syndicates treated this hall like kindling," she says. "If a thing cracked, they nailed a board over it and raised the rent." She swings the door once more and listens. "It's a good sound, timber settling under folk who mend what breaks. I didn't expect to hear it again in my lifetime, and I've a long one."

choices.label: Hand her a fresh brass handle for the final suite
choices.res: You hand her the brass handle for the last suite. She weighs it in her palm, grunts her approval, and drives the screws home in four turns each. Then she nods to you, once. "Best boss this hall's had in thirty years," she says. "That's not much of a compliment, mind. You've seen what the others were like."

choices.label: Tell her she doesn't have to carry every hammer alone now
choices.res: You tell her that she doesn't have to carry every hammer herself any more. Brynna snorts. Then, for about a second, she leans her shoulder against yours. It's like being leaned on by a wall. "Maybe," she says. "I'll think on it. Just you keep folk's boots off my varnish while I do."

brynna.title: Boiler Warmth

image.comp: resting on a thick wool bench beside a glowing cast-iron dwarven boiler stove, unlaced leather apron, unexpectedly tender smile
image.setting: warm timber hearth parlor inside Ironwood Hall at night

2.text:
Rain is hammering on the tin of the eaves. Down in the cellar the old dwarven boiler is ticking over, and the whole room is warm and smells of cedar.

Brynna unbuckles her tool belt and lets it drop on the hearth rug. It lands heavily. Her carpenter's apron follows it. Then she undoes the top two studs of her collar with one thick finger, and she watches you while she does it.

"Good timber holds when the weight comes on," she says. Her voice is low. "It doesn't creak about it and it doesn't shift. You can't tell which wood will do that until you've loaded it." She sits down on the wool rug by the stove and looks up at you across the firelight. "I've loaded you a fair bit this year, boss, and you've held. Come down here. I've had my hands on this hall all season, and I'd like to put them on something else."

image.comp: sitting on a wool rug beside a glowing stove looking up at him, tool belt dropped on the hearth, steady heavy-lidded gaze
image.wear: a work shirt with the collar undone

brynna.text:
Rain is hammering on the tin of the eaves. Down in the cellar the old dwarven boiler is ticking over, and the whole room is warm and smells of cedar.

Brynna has finished for the day. She wipes the oak dust off her knuckles with a rag, pours two pewter mugs of mulled cider from the pan on the stove, and pushes one along the bench to you. She doesn't say anything for a while. She is not much of a talker, and you've learned to wait.

"I've built a fair few things," she says in the end. She is looking at the boiler and not at you. "There were mills and bridges, and I did the roof of half this row. I'd finish, and somebody else would move in, and I'd go." She turns the mug around in her hands. "This is the first roof I ever nailed down and then stopped under. It was yours all winter, and it was mine as well." Her ears have gone red. "It was worth every splinter. That's all I wanted to say."

choices.label: Pull up close beside her by the warm stove
choices.res: Brynna laughs, low in her chest. She gets a fistful of your hoodie in each hard hand and pulls you down onto the rug beside her.

else.res: You stretch out on the bench by the stove and swap carpenter's jokes. Hers are very dry, and they are mostly about masons. You don't understand most of them. She laughs at all of yours anyway, and by the time the rain stops the sun is drying the porch boards.

choices.label: Rub the knots out of her sore forearms after work
choices.res: You take her forearm in both hands and dig your thumbs into the muscle. It is like kneading a ship's cable. She groans out loud, with no shame at all, and her head tips back against the wall. "Fine," she mutters. "I'll grant that those soft city hands are good for something. Do the other one."

maren.title: Secret Blends

image.comp: measuring drops of amber oil into tiny labelled glass vials under hanging orchids, glancing up with a sly half-lidded smile
image.setting: sunlit apothecary potting bench inside The Glass Conservatory

maren.text:
The morning sun is coming through the fogged glass and turning the mist in the Conservatory to gold. Maren is at her workbench under the orchids with a row of tiny vials and a glass dropper. She is bottling the first of the dusk-orchid oil.

She has you holding two brass bowls. You can't put either of them down. She knows that perfectly well.

She corks one plain vial without a label, steps in close, and tucks it into your shirt pocket. She leaves her fingers there a moment longer than she needs to. Her ears tilt forward.

"That one isn't for the censers," she says in her low voice. "I made it for you. I call it 'quiet night'. It has cedar in it, and a little jasmine, and one thing I'm not going to tell you." She pats the pocket. "It keeps the pulse steady. This whole town has been working you ragged, Sam, and I've watched it. Somebody ought to look after the gardener."

choices.label: Ask her to test a drop right on your wrist
choices.res: You ask her to try it on you. She takes your wrist, turns it over, and puts a single drop on the pulse. It smells of cedar and night jasmine and warm skin. Maren bends her head over it, and you feel her smile against your knuckles. "There," she murmurs. "It worked already, didn't it? You've stopped holding your breath."

choices.label: Offer to label the Spice Guild reserve crates with her
choices.res: She hands you her best quill, and the two of you label the reserve crates for the Spice Guild. She spends the whole hour making up names for the new blends. Each is more scandalous than the last, and she watches your ears while she reads them out. Three of them go on the jars. You will have to explain them to customers.

maren.title: Under Glass

image.comp: curled lazily along a velvet chaise under a moonlit glass dome, beckoning with one hand, languid inviting eyes
image.setting: midnight moonlit dome of The Glass Conservatory with glowing hanging censers

2.text:
Both moons are up, and the arched glass overhead has gone silver. The censers are burning low, and their smoke lies along the floor in thin gold layers.

Maren is stretched out on the crimson chaise. Her dress is undone down the front, and she is lying on her side, with her tail curled over her bare calves. She is holding up a ribbon between two fingers. It's the one off the door. She has taken the 'open' sign down.

"The glass keeps every scent in. Do you remember?" she says. "I've had 'quiet night' in the censers for an hour. It's the strong one. I didn't make it to steady anything." The tip of her tail flicks. Her amber eyes have gone dark, and her ears are pricked forward. "The door's latched, Sam. Breathe in, and then come here. I've been waiting on this chaise since sunset, and foxes aren't patient."

image.comp: lying on her side along a crimson chaise, tail curled over her bare calves, holding a ribbon up between two fingers, ears pricked
image.wear: a dress undone down the front

maren.text:
Both moons are up, and the arched glass overhead has gone silver. The censers are burning low. Their smoke lies along the floor in thin gold layers and curls when you walk through it.

Maren is on the velvet chaise by the fountain with her shoes off. She beckons you over lazily. You sit, and she lays her tail across your knees as if it were a blanket.

"I've been thinking about owners," she says. "I've known a few. To most of them a house like this is so many coins with a lock on the door. They can tell you what a suite earns in a night, and they've never once sat in it." She tips her head back to look at the orchids hanging over you. "You watered those. It was in your first week, when nobody had asked you to, and you got it wrong. I had to go round after you." Her eyes slide over to yours, half shut. "Don't think I didn't notice, Sam. I notice everything that grows."

choices.label: Join her on the velvet chaise beneath the glass dome
choices.res: Her tail brushes over your wrists, soft and warm. Then Maren takes hold of the front of your shirt and pulls you down toward her. Her skin smells of jasmine.

else.res: "A good garden deserves tending," you say. Maren hums, pleased, and settles her tail more comfortably across your knee. She stays like that for the rest of the evening, warm against your side, naming the orchids for you one by one in a voice that could put a whole city to sleep.

choices.label: Drink plum tea together watching mist gather on the dome
choices.res: You drink plum tea and watch the mist gather on the inside of the dome and run down in slow lines. She tells you which plants are asleep and which are only pretending. The warm, sweet air undoes every knot in your back, one at a time. You are still there when the stars go pale above the glass.

vivienne.title: Passing Marks

image.comp: perched on the corner of a dark mahogany lectern grading parchment with a slim fountain pen, poised knowing half-smile over spectacles
image.setting: quiet candlelit lecture salon at The Velvet Lyceum

vivienne.text:
The Academy board has stopped writing letters. Half of Academy Square is angling for an invitation to the next soirée. Vivienne has not said a word about any of it.

This afternoon she sends for you. She is sitting on the corner of the lectern in the empty hall with a pen in her hand, and she has a card in front of her. It is a folded evaluation card, the kind she fills in for the staff every month. This one is sealed in the Lyceum's own red wax.

Your name is on the front.

"Posture," she reads, without looking up from her spectacles. "Still slouches. This is marginal, and I have noted it before." She turns the card over. "Judgment under pressure. Fairness to staff. Ability to silence three pompous governors before the wine was finished." She caps her pen. "Exemplary, in each case. I do not use that word often." Her grey eyes come up to yours. "You may consider yourself graduated, Sam. I confess that I didn't expect it."

choices.label: Ask what extra-credit seminar comes next
choices.res: You ask what the extra-credit seminar is. Vivienne taps her riding crop once against the edge of the blotter. Her eyes glint. "Do be careful, Mr. Takahashi," she says. "Private tuition is a good deal more demanding than the general course. I set the reading myself. I have never yet had a student finish it."

choices.label: Frame the wax-sealed card above the salon door
choices.res: You have the card framed and hung over the salon door, wax seal and all, where every patron walks under it. Vivienne looks up at it. Then she laughs, behind her hand. It's a real laugh, and it lasts one breath. You have never heard it before. "Absurd man," she says. "Leave it there. Let them all see what my standards produce."

vivienne.title: After Seminar

image.comp: standing beside tall gilded mirrors setting her spectacles down next to a brandy decanter, cool composure with a hint of warmth
image.setting: private velvet mirror suite at The Velvet Lyceum at night

2.text:
The last carriage has gone out of the courtyard. The candles in the mirror suite are burning down, and each one is repeated four times in the gilded glass.

Vivienne takes off her spectacles and sets them down beside the brandy decanter. Then she reaches up and draws the pins out of her chignon, one after another, and lays them in a row. Her dark hair comes down over her bare shoulders. You see it in all four mirrors at once.

"There are no students," she says. "There are no callers, and there isn't a syllabus." The cool voice is the same, but it is slower and lower than usual. She turns to face you, and she is smiling. It is a wicked smile, and she has never let it out in the lecture hall. "I have been composed for fourteen hours, Sam. I am very tired of it. Lock the door. Then come here and help me to stop."

image.comp: standing before gilded mirrors with hairpins laid in a row, hair loose over bare shoulders, spectacles set aside, slow wicked smile

vivienne.text:
The last carriage has gone out of the courtyard. The candles in the mirror suite are burning down, and each one is repeated four times in the gilded glass.

Vivienne takes off her spectacles and sets them down beside the brandy decanter. She pinches the bridge of her nose. It is the first time you have seen her look tired, and she has allowed you to see it.

"I should tell you why I left," she says. "I was very good at my work. I taught the daughters of this city to pour tea and say nothing. It took me eight years to understand that I was training them to be furniture." She pours two glasses and gives you one. "I came here expecting common coin and coarse manners. I thought I would be the sharpest thing in the building." She almost smiles. "You have made it into a place where a woman is paid to be clever. I had not thought that could be done. I was wrong, and I dislike that. I wanted you to know."

choices.label: Lock the gilded mirror suite behind you
choices.res: You lock the door. Vivienne takes your collar between two fingers and walks you backward, a step at a time, until the backs of your knees meet the velvet divan in front of the mirror.

else.res: "Good faculty sets the tone," you tell her, and hand her back her glass. Vivienne looks at you for a moment without her spectacles. Then she touches the rim of her glass to yours. "Always, Sam," she says. It is the warmest you have ever heard her.

choices.label: Let her dictate the quiet evening pace over old plum wine
choices.res: You leave the pace of the evening to her, and she is good at setting one. She pours the old plum wine and takes the soirée apart for you, guest by guest. She is wickedly accurate, and you laugh until your ribs hurt. With her in it, an empty salon turns into the liveliest hour of your week.
